message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Physical & Chemical Properties**

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Common isotopes** | ¹H (protium, ~99.98 %), ²H (deuterium, ~0.02 %) – stable; ³H (tritium) – radioactive (half‑life ≈12.32 y) |
| **Atomic mass** | 1.00794 u (average weighted by natural abundance) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Second ionization energy** | 27.211 eV (2625 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| **Electron affinity** | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ (negative, meaning it does *not* readily accept an extra electron) |
| **Molecular weight (H₂)** | 2.01588 g mol⁻¹ |
| **Boiling point (at 1 atm)** | –252.87 °C (20.44 K) |
| **Melting point (at 1 atm)** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 kg m⁻³) |
| **Specific heat capacity (gas, 25 °C)** | 28.836 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| **Heat of formation (gas)** | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| **Bond dissociation energy (H–H)** | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Acidity/basicity** | Very weak acid (pKa ≈ 35) when protonated; very weak base (pKb ≈ 35) when deprotonated |
| **Flammability** | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (range 4–75 % vol.) |
| **Solubility in water** | 7.9 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C (≈0.009 mol L⁻¹) |
| **Reactivity** | Reacts slowly with metals (forming hydrides); reacts vigorously with halogens (forming HX) under UV or heat; reacts with oxygen to form water (exothermic). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – key in astrophysics. |
| **Uses** | Fuel cell fuel, rocket propellant (liquid hydrogen), ammonia synthesis (Haber process), hydrogenation reactions, metal processing, laboratory standard gas. |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element** – lowest density, high specific energy content per unit mass.
- **Highly reactive** – forms covalent bonds easily; forms strong H–H bond but also forms many compounds (e.g., H₂O, NH₃).
- **Isotopic variants** – deuterium used in nuclear fusion research; tritium used in nuclear weapons and fusion experiments.
- **Spectroscopic importance** – hydrogen spectral lines are fundamental to astronomy and quantum mechanics.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property!
